previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for a scheduled bronchoscopy with balloon dilation of the trachea and mainstem bronchi, along with tracheostomy tube exchange, due to recurrent tracheobronchial stenosis from Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome and relapsing polychondritis. The procedure was performed without complications, with successful dilation to 12 mm in the trachea, 8 mm in the right bronchus, and 10 mm in the left. A standard Portex 9 tracheostomy tube was placed due to compression preventing use of a custom tube. Post-procedure, he experienced mild pain managed with acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and oxycodone, and was briefly ventilated for analgesia. He developed mild wheezing on hospital day two, treated with a single dose of IV decadron. He remained stable, with clear lungs on imaging and no signs of infection. He was discharged home on day three with all home medications continued and follow-up planned with interventional pulmonary and rheumatology.
